newsitem.title: USA: California settles with tobacco company.
newsitem.headline: California settles with tobacco company.

text.p: California Attorney General Dan Lungren Thursday said the state reached a settlement with tobacco company Brooke Group Ltd. to recoup health care costs.

Under terms of the settlement, Brooke, parent of Liggett Tobacco Co., has agreed to reimburse California for public health costs incurred as a result of smoking as well as providing internal documents that could help the state sue others in the tobacco industry.
"The real fruit of this settlement will be in the potential evidence that California will now gain access to," Lungren told reporters at a news conference here.

"Liggett will provide my office with internal industry documents which may demonstrate ... that the tobacco industry has targeted minors with advertising, manipulated nicotine levels and is engaged in illegal fruadulent conduct."
The terms of the agreement are substantially the same as those reached between Brooke and 22 other states on March 20.

In that agreement Liggett agreed to place warnings on its cigarettes stating that "smoking is addictive" and that it will pay 25 percent of its pretax income for the next 25 years into a settlement fund to compensate state health care programs and fund counter-market advertising.
What makes the California settlement unusual is that unlike the other 22 states it never sued Brooke due to the state's Brown-Lockyer Civil Liability Reform Act of 1987.
The controversial Brown-Lockyer law exempts tobacco companies from product liability lawsuits in California.

Lungren said the settlement would allow his office to pursue lawsuits against other tobacco companies but only if California's legislature overturns the act. If the law stands he said his office would just be wasting money in pursuing the tobacco industry.
"It would truly be a shame if damning evidence were to come into our possesion only for us to be stymied by a special tobacco exemption deal cut some 10 years ago," Lungren said.
While he said he was willing to pursue lawsuits against the tobacco industry the best solution would be a national settlement brokered by Congress in Washington.
"A global settlement is preferable to an endless parade of lawsuits clogging state and federal courts," Lungren said.
He said a final settlement should include assurances that minors would not be targeted and that the tobacco companies would cooperate in making a less harmfull product.

Brooke said Thusday it has also reached a separate settlement in principle with San Francisco and 10 surrounding counties regarding to production of documents and other elements related to tobacco industry lawsuits.

Liggett Group, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd., broke ranks in March with other tobacco companies by agreeing to settle with 22 state attorneys general who sued the industry to recoup smoking-related health care costs.
